work.informant: No individual informant is named in the consulted edition. The story is presented as a traditional folk narrative collected and edited by the Brothers Grimm.
work.publication_characteristics: The 1819 edition names the Brothers Grimm, was published during both of their lifetimes, and is not anonymous, pseudonymous, or posthumous. The 1857 seventh edition is a different later text and was not used.
work.source_transcription_quality: The source page identifies the 1819 second edition, volume 1, pages 141–145, and states that the text was proofread twice against the source and follows the original spelling.
work.scan_use: The scan pages were used only to verify the historical text. None of the scans, page images, or historical illustrations are embedded in the BookCheef publication.

public_domain_analysis.EU_EEA: Directive 2006/116/EC, Article 1(1)–(2): life plus 70 years, calculated from the death of the last surviving co-author. The last surviving named editor died in 1863; the term ended 31 December 1933 and the work has been public domain since 1 January 1934.
public_domain_analysis.Germany: UrhG §§64–65 and §69: 70 years after the last surviving joint author, calculated from the end of the calendar year. No §71 posthumous first-publication right applies because the 1819 text was published during the editors' lifetimes.
public_domain_analysis.Netherlands: Government guidance states that copyright expires 70 years after the creator's death, counted from 1 January of the following year.
public_domain_analysis.Poland: Copyright and Related Rights Act, consolidated text Dz.U. 2025 poz. 24, Article 36(1) for joint works and Article 39 for calculation. Article 40 is marked repealed in the current consolidated text.
public_domain_analysis.Mexico: Federal Law on Copyright, current WIPO Lex version 2026, Article 29(I): life plus 100 years for co-authored works, counted from the death of the last co-author. Even this longer term ended by 31 December 1963.
public_domain_analysis.United_States: The source edition was published in 1819, before 1 January 1931; the Commons source scans also carry the public-domain designation for the United States.
